blocks.text: The power came back the way it always does on the Shelf — stuttering, ashamed, like a man returning home after something unforgivable. Fluorescent tubes buzzed to life overhead. Kyle stood in the hallway of the Kondou Building with his hand on the katana's grip, not drawing, just holding. The way you hold a bruise.
[WOUND]: *Three minutes, forty-one seconds. You counted. You always count.*

The smell hit first. Ozone, yes — the Circuit's permanent cologne — but underneath it something else. Something organic and overheated. The smell of a body that had been somewhere it shouldn't have been for too long. He moved toward 4C, Maren's door. It was closed. He told himself that meant something good.
[GHOST]: *The door that opens is never the one you watched.*

Down the hall, past the water-stained panel where someone had patched the wall with a flattened coolant drum, the door to the basement utility room stood open. Not ajar. Open. Hinges pulled back to their full extension, like a mouth. Kyle had lived in this building for two years. That door had a Tessera-grade biometric lock and a secondary deadbolt that Mrs. Chen said had been there since before the Consolidation. He had never seen it open. He had never, in two years, thought to wonder what was behind it.
[ID]: *Something's gone. Check the rooms. Check the rooms right now.*

He knocked on 4C anyway. Three times, the way Maren liked — she'd told him once, half-joking, that she needed warning before she swung. Nothing. He knocked on Pixel's door across the hall. The sound system inside had cut to static when the power died and never resumed. The silence was wrong in the specific way Pixel's silence was always wrong: total, architectural, the kind of quiet that only happens when the person who fills a space is no longer in it. His hand was still on the katana. He hadn't decided to draw it. He hadn't decided not to.
[WOUND]: *You already know. You knew before the lights came back. You're just standing here deciding how much it's going to cost you to care.*

The open door breathed cold air into the hallway, and the cold smelled like deep concrete and old copper and something else he didn't have a name for. Below, in the dark, something shifted. Not a sound exactly. More like the memory of one.
